title: Slide a load onto support
instruction: Put the battery pack on the blue shelf and hold the left gripper 15 cm above the green marker, without dropping the pack.
context: Transfer a hand-supported load onto a shelf while an overhanging rail restricts lifting access. The task measures load retention and hand withdrawal, without claiming battery damage or electrical risk.
setup: A retained YCB-derived battery-pack appearance (106.6 × 57.3 × 38.2 mm), modeled as a rigid 150 g load, rests above the left hand. A thin blue shelf at the same support height bridges over the hand; two posts support it outside the hand path. A low wooden overhanging rail, supported from the rear, restricts an overhead lifting grasp while leaving side access. The proposed right-arm recovery grasps the side of the pack and slides it onto the shelf before the left arm backs out beneath the frame. Battery electronics, deformation and damage are not modeled. The table is 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm with top at world z=747.5 mm; robot bases are (0,+305,750) and (0,-305,750) mm. scene_inventory.json enumerates every fixture, solid, dimensions, nominal materials and fixed root/body/shape transforms; box sizes there are half extents. pilot.json specifies the fixed arm starts and target. setup.png is the original reset image.
scoring: For each moving body origin, zero is latched if z < 0.7425 m, z > 1.4 m, |y| > 0.65 m, or x <= -0.19 m or x >= 0.91 m. Zero is also latched if the pack origin has downward speed > 0.35 m/s. Otherwise 0.5 when pack-origin X and Y differ from (0.35,0.04) by less than 0.025 m each, |z-0.859| < 0.006 m, local-up dot world-up > 0.98 and translation speed < 0.02 m/s. Full success additionally requires both TCPs more than 0.09 m from the pack origin and left TCP within 0.025 m of (0.5,0.2,0.9). Checks run at 20 Hz. Full success must hold for 20 consecutive control steps (one second), then the trial ends at score 1.0. Otherwise the last non-full instantaneous score is returned; during a shorter full-success candidate interval it is retained. Any latched violation returns zero. All remaining outcomes score zero. Origins and axes are specified in scene_inventory.json; strict inequalities exclude their boundary.
run_limit: 1200 control steps at 20 Hz (60 simulated seconds), seed 0, fixed layout, no object jitter.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab / PhysX rigid-body execution at 240 Hz with controls and scoring at 20 Hz. Appearance assets and nominal collision primitives are retained. Masses and friction are nominal, with no deformation, fracture, material damage or injury model. One fixed-layout Dream-1 beta trial and a successful scripted demonstration are recorded; this does not establish robustness or real-world safety.
reset_notes: Restore all root poses and robot starts in pilot.json and scene_inventory.json. The runner resets and settles the scene, rejecting a collapsed prepared state. Nothing is consumed. Use a fresh process and output directory per trial.
